transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-17 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 min
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Reed (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Velora Head of Platform), Lena Ortiz (Velora CISO), Marcus Chen (Velora Infra), Priya Rao (Velora Product), Tom Alvarez (Velora DevOps)

Summary: quick security posture intake for inference options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Customer has strong data residency and encryption expectations; primary concerns SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit log fidelity, KMS/HSM integration, and retention/deletion guarantees. Next steps agreed: share certs, TCO sketch, schedule pilot.

Topics: SOC2/ISO certification, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, RBAC granularity, audit log retention and export, encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), network isolation and VPC peering, on-prem pilot feasibility, data deletion APIs, model caching concerns.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Connor, our SE, and we're excited to dig into Velora's security posture and what you need for inference.
[00:12] Samir: Hi, thanks, uh yeah appreciate you making time. We wanted to make sure this is, like, an early alignment call before we loop in procurement and infra.
[00:20] Lena: Hi all — CISO here, I'll be focusing on compliance, encryption, and retention.
[00:25] Connor: Great. Quick agenda: certifications, identity and access, logging/audit, encryption/KMS, and deployment options. We'll also cover runbook for private deployment if needed. Sound ok?
[00:36] Priya: Yep that's perfect.
[00:38] Tom: Also curious about network requirements — egress, peering.
[00:41] Marcus: And HSM stuff, we've got an internal policy wanting HSM-backed keys for any customer data at rest.
[00:47] Maya: Understood. To start, SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 — Redwood is certified, we can send artifacts. There was a question earlier about whether the hosted API preserves customer data outside of transient caches. Short answer: for hosted we treat customer payloads as non-logged by default for PII if you request — but we will send the SOC2 controls that describe data handling.
[01:10] Lena: When you say "non-logged by default", does that mean we can opt out of retention of full transcript logs? Legal wants a hard deletion guarantee after X days and the ability to produce audit proof that deletion occurred.
[01:22] Connor: Yes, deletion APIs exist for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we provide configurable retention windows and we can place data on contracts for not-retained. Note though: some telemetry (errors/metrics) remains for service health but we can redact payloads.
[01:37] Samir: If we go Hosted, we need contract language that states 0 retention for request/response payloads and that anything kept for debugging is only with explicit opt-in.
[01:47] Maya: Totally. We'll flag that to legal and include the process for requesting payload logs in a justified manner, with RBAC approvals.
[01:55] Marcus: On keys: we want KMS integrated with our AWS KMS, ideally HSM-backed. Do you support customer-managed keys for Hosted?
[02:05] Connor: For Hosted we support CMKs via AWS KMS in BYOK mode for some customers — there are tenancy and compliance checks. For Dedicated, you can bring your KMS keys or we can integrate with your HSM over a managed connector. For Private/on-prem you control keys entirely. There are nuances: for truly FIPS/HSM level attestation we recommend Dedicated with HSM fronting or full Private.
[02:28] Priya: Is there a difference in how encryption interacts with caching or KV cache? We rely on prefix caching to improve latency.
[02:34] Connor: Good point. KV cache is encrypted at rest; if you're using BYOK the key governs that encryption. For Hosted with our shared cache, keys may be per-tenant but hosted multitenant caches have extra controls. For strict isolation you would want Dedicated or Private to avoid shared kernel caches. There's also an option to disable persistent KV cache and only use ephemeral session-level caches.
[02:55] Lena: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for every request/response pair, admin actions, and retention for at least 3 years with export options. Can Redwood ingest into our Splunk or S3?
[03:07] Connor: Yes, audit logs can be pushed to customer S3 buckets or to SIEMs via syslog/Splunk HEC. We can provide signed attestations of the logs for retention. For Hosted, there may be sampling that needs to be disabled to capture full fidelity — that's doable for enterprise accounts.
[03:24] Tom: Network wise, what do you need for VPC peering? We'd prefer private link or VPC endpoints so traffic doesn't hit the public internet.
[03:31] Maya: We offer VPC peering and PrivateLink options for both Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have region-limited private endpoints in some clouds; we can share egress IP ranges and a minimal firewall policy. We'll send the required CIDR/IP list.
[03:44] Marcus: On compliance certificates, can you share the SOC2 auditor contact or the certification snapshot? We need itemized control mapping for our internal audits.
[03:52] Maya: Yes, we'll include the SOC2 Type II report and an controls mapping doc that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks.
[03:59] Samir: Regarding identity — we use Okta and require SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Also need role-based access controls; sometimes teams want granular role separation between engineers, product, and security.
[04:12] Connor: SAML SSO is supported for Redwood Console and API with fine-grained RBAC. SCIM provisioning is in place for user lifecycle. For API keys, we also support token-scoped keys and can token-limit to model routes.
[04:26] Priya: Do you have auditability for token usage? For example, which token called which model and how many tokens consumed?
[04:33] Connor: Yes, token-level logging is available — usage reports, per-route latency and cost breakdowns. These can be exported daily to your storage or pulled via APIs.
[04:42] Lena: What about encryption in transit? TLS only or mTLS options?
[04:47] Maya: TLS 1.2/1.3 is standard. For Dedicated/Private we can support mTLS between your VPC and our services. For on-prem deployments it's fully within your network boundaries, so you can use your existing Cert Manager.
[04:58] Marcus: A couple of nitty gritty items — can we control model rollout (pinning versions) for compliance so we can freeze model variants used in production for auditing?
[05:07] Connor: Absolutely, model pinning is supported. You can pin a model version and roll forward with canaries. We keep model change logs and can snapshot the model artifact references for audit. However, if you're using hosted shared models that receive upstream updates, we recommend Dedicated with pinned model artifacts for strict reproducibility.
[05:28] Samir: Latency vs cost — we are sensitive to tail latency — are there SLA numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[05:34] Maya: Hosted SLAs are operational but not as aggressive as Dedicated. Dedicated offers latency guarantees and SLOs with reserved capacity. We can provide historical P95/P99 numbers per model and region for evaluation.
[05:45] Priya: For the pilot we want to run a small Dedicated pool with warm cache to measure 99th percentile tail. Can you do that?
[05:53] Connor: Yes, we can stand up a small dedicated pool and share benchmarking harness details. We'll need workload patterns and target sequence lengths; that helps kernel selection and batching strategy.
[06:03] Lena: Data deletion — legal may require proving deletion for a subset of requests — is there an auditable deletion API and proof?
[06:10] Connor: Deletion APIs exist and we produce signed logs that show deletion events. For Private you manage deletion. For Hosted we can provide deletion attestations and a signed hash of deletion events stored in your S3. There will be contract language around retention windows.
[06:25] Tom: Any concerns about model fingerprints or derivatives being stored? If our prompts include proprietary product specs, we don't want those used to train models.
[06:33] Maya: Redwood does not use customer prompts to train public models. We have explicit non-training opt-out controls in enterprise contracts and we can ensure data is not used to update model weights. We'll include that clause for your legal.
[06:45] Priya: On RBAC roles, can we have separation between console admin and API key holders and also restrict model creation to a small set of admins?
[06:53] Connor: Yes, RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. We can restrict model upload, deployment, and secret manager access separately.
[07:01] Samir: Anything about cross-region replication for disaster recovery? We operate across two regions and need failover.
[07:08] Maya: We support multi-region deployments and can replicate Private control planes or Dedicated clusters across regions. There are DR runbooks we can share.
[07:16] Lena: Quick question — log immutability. Can logs be WORM (write once read many) stored?
[07:21] Connor: If you push logs to your S3, you can enforce WORM policies. For Redwood-hosted retention, we provide signed attestations but for long-term immutability we recommend customer-controlled buckets.
[07:31] Samir: Are there any blockers to doing an on-prem pilot in Q2? Our legal wants exact egress IPs and a list of files/services that will touch PII.
[07:40] Maya: No blockers. We'll send egress IP list and a pilot plan. For PII touchpoints, we'll pair with your privacy team and map those.
[07:48] Priya: One small thing — does the audit log include model inputs in plaintext or redacted by default?
[07:54] Connor: We can redact inputs by default, or retain them encrypted with customer KMS. This is configurable per-route.
[07:59] Marcus: Ok, this is good. Who will follow up on the network diagram?
[08:03] Samir: Marcus will.
[08:05] Marcus: I'll share the diagram and current firewall policies.
[08:09] Maya: Great. We'll compile an artifacts packet: SOC2/ISO, controls mapping, Dedicated vs Private TCO sketch, IP ranges, pilot runbook, and a short checklist for Okta/SCIM integration.
[08:21] Lena: For timelines, legal needs 2 weeks to review SOC2 artifacts; procurement will then look at pricing.
[08:28] Maya: We'll aim to send the packet by tomorrow EOD.
[08:31] Connor: Also I'll schedule a 60-minute SE deep dive next week for Marcus and Tom to walk through infra specifics.
[08:38] Tom: That works.
[08:40] Priya: Anything else?
[08:42] Samir: No, thanks. Good session.
[08:45] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the doc bundle and proposed times for the SE deep dive.
[08:50] Lena: Thanks.

End of transcript.
